meta.title: Snow removal and plowing in Linden, MI | Grand Scapes
meta.description: Snow plowing and salting in Linden, MI by Grand Scapes: driveways and walks cleared with our own trucks, on city streets and Fenton Township roads alike.

hero.title: Linden drives, **plowed edge to edge.**
hero.lede: Grand Scapes plows Linden driveways with our own trucks and puts ice melt down on walks and steps. The city's crew clears city streets and the county clears the township roads; your drive and walks are the part we handle.

local.title: Who plows Linden's streets and **the roads around them.**
local.intro: Inside the city, the public works department handles snow and ice removal on city streets, including the city's dirt roads. Just past the city limits, Fenton Township roads belong to the Genesee County Road Commission, which reaches subdivision streets after everything else.

points.title: No overnight street parking in winter
points.body: The city's fall newsletter says no on-street parking from November 1 to March 31, starting at 2:30 in the morning; check with City Hall for the exact hours. A clear street lets the plow work curb to curb, and a drive that is already open means the car has somewhere to go.

points.title: Dirt roads and soft edges
points.body: Some city streets are dirt, and a drive that meets one or a gravel shoulder has soft edges. Show those to Rob on his visit, so the plow knows where the drive stops.

points.title: Township roads around the city
points.body: On Fenton Township roads around the city, the county's winter policy puts subdivision streets and gravel local roads at the end of its list, plowed and graded but left snow covered, with no overtime. Linden Road is one of the primary roads that comes first.

points.title: Salt and the river
points.body: Linden sits on the Shiawassee, and the road commission notes that salt runs off into lakes and streams. MSU Extension adds that salt piles up in beds beside walks and drives. Ice melt goes on the walks and steps, not across the yard.

logistics.title: How a Linden snow season gets set up.
body: Before the first storm, Rob walks the property and looks at the drive, the walks and steps, where you park, and where the snow can go without landing in a flower bed or out in the street. Then he explains the residential package options.

The trucks are our own white pickups with stainless plows, and a walk behind spreader puts down ice melt on walks and steps. Snow is piled on your property, because state law says snow, ice or slush may not be deposited on any roadway.

facts.label: Winter street parking
facts.value: None Nov 1 to Mar 31, check hours

faq.q: Do you plow driveways in Linden?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes plows residential driveways in the City of Linden and on the Fenton Township roads around it with our own trucks, and we [salt walks and steps](/salting-and-sidewalks/) as well. Call [(810) 990-3040](tel:+18109903040) or [text Rob](sms:+18109903040) for a free estimate.

faq.q: Can I park on the street in Linden during the winter?
faq.a: Not overnight. The city's fall 2026 newsletter lists no on-street parking from November 1 through March 31, beginning at 2:30 in the morning. Confirm the exact hours with City Hall before the first snow.

faq.q: Who plows the roads just outside the city?
faq.a: The Genesee County Road Commission plows the Fenton Township roads around Linden. US-23 and primary roads like Linden Road come first, then local roads, then subdivision streets, and the road commission asks people to allow 48 hours for local roads after a storm.

faq.q: Will a plow damage my mailbox or lawn edge?
faq.a: It can happen with any plow, ours or the road crew's. The road commission encourages owners to check their mailbox and post before winter and replace a worn one. Marking the drive edges before the ground freezes keeps a blade off the grass and the curb.
